page: Microsoft Azure D48nls_v6 is a low-memory, network-optimized general purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor providing 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores at clock speeds reaching up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, with hardware support for advanced vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AMX. The instance is paired with 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reflects strong compute, decompression, and throughput performance. In PassMark testing, the instance recorded a CPU score of 56,283.8 and an extended instructions score of 54,193.39, placing it in the top 25% of measured systems. While stress-ng single-core (1,928.89) and multi-core (40,816.15) scores sit in the middle 50%, multi-threaded data handling remains robust, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 275.3 GB/sec and static web serving throughput hitting 73.21 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate top-quartile performance for large-block uncached operations, measuring 252.33 GB/sec for reads and 104.24 GB/sec for writes.

CPU-based machine learning inference shows solid results, highlighted by small model (135M) text generation reaching top-tier throughput at 337.85 tokens/sec, and 7B model prompt processing achieving 215.8 tokens/sec. The primary operational tradeoff of the D48nls_v6 is its non-standard 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside the total absence of bundled local storage. For deployments requiring massive memory footprints or fast local scratch disks, standard D-series or memory-optimized instances are better suited. However, for compute-heavy microservices, network-focused workloads, static web delivery, and distributed CPU-based inference clusters, it delivers high processing density without the cost overhead of unutilized RAM.

It is provisioned with 96.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), a 260 MB L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. The instance lacks bundled local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results place the instance in the top 25% for PassMark CPU performance, large-block memory bandwidth, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (275.3 GB/sec), and static web serving throughput (73.21 GB/sec). With a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, the D48nls_v6 provides high compute density for workloads such as static web serving, network processing, containerized microservices, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
